name: Onset of Tithe Obligation (Shiur Malachah / Gmar Melachah)
notes: Covers when produce becomes obligated in tithes based on completion of agricultural work (threshing floor equivalent) — the specific trigger-point for each type of produce

name: Casual/Chance Eating Exempt from Tithes (Achilat Arai)
notes: The principle that eating produce in a casual, incidental manner (not as a formal meal) exempts one from tithing; contrasted with keva eating

name: Worker's Right to Eat from Produce (Po'el Ochel)
notes: The Torah-mandated right of a hired agricultural worker to eat from the produce he harvests and the interaction of that right with tithe obligations

name: Courtyard that Obligates Tithes (Chatzer haMechayevet Maaser)
notes: Which type of courtyard renders produce brought into it liable for tithes — rules about the nature of the courtyard as a formal domain

name: Stages of Fruit Ripeness for Tithe Liability
notes: Specific determinations of when each type of fruit or vegetable reaches the stage at which tithes become obligatory (bichur/peel stage for various species)

name: Selling Produce to One Untrusted in Tithes (Am HaAretz)
notes: Prohibitions on selling untithed produce or byproducts to those suspected of not tithing, and related rules about straw, grape pulp, and olive peat

name: Tithe Obligations for Produce from Syria
notes: Special rules governing tithe obligations for produce acquired in Syria, depending on whether the land was purchased

name: Grape-Skin Wine (Yayin Poret / Tirosh miGefanim)
notes: Rules about tithe obligations for secondary wine made by adding water to grape skins

name: Ants Carrying Grain Near Completed Pile
notes: Whether grain dragged by ants from a completed tithe-liable pile overnight is itself liable for tithes

name: Exotic or Foreign Produce Exempt from Tithes
notes: Certain foreign species (e.g., Balbeck garlic, Rikpa onions, Egyptian lentils) exempt from tithes due to their origin

name: Seeds of Vegetables Not Eaten — Exempt from Tithes
hebrew: זרעי ירקות שאינם נאכלים פטורים ממעשר
notes: Seeds of garden vegetables that are inedible are exempt from tithes even if the parent plant was terumah

name: Tithing Dill and Coriander (Seeds, Plants, and Pods)
notes: Dispute about whether seeds, plant, and pods of dill and coriander are each separately subject to tithing

name: Separating Terumah Before Work is Completed
notes: Effect on chance-eating exemption when terumah is separated from produce before its agricultural work has been completed

name: Tree Overhanging from One Domain to Another (Tithe Implications)
hebrew: אילן הנוטה לחצר אחרת לגבי מעשר
notes: Rules about when fruit from a tree overhanging from garden to courtyard (or from Israel to outside) is liable for tithes, based on root location

name: Jerusalem Rule: Tithe Determined by Branch Location
notes: Special rule that for trees overhanging Jerusalem's walls, tithe liability is determined by branch location rather than root location
